prerequisites: Basic knowledge of chemistry, computer science, electricity, physics, and statistics is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and skillfully manage legislation on Occupational Safety and Health.
Acquire general knowledge of the international standard for Prevention Management ISO 45001.
Apply quantitative and qualitative methods for the analysis and evaluation of occupational risks.
Possess basic theoretical and practical knowledge in the following three disciplines of Occupational Safety and Health: Safety at Work, Industrial Hygiene, and Applied Ergonomics and Psychosociology.
Possess specific knowledge of national, European, and/or international legislation and regulations in the field of Industrial Safety, with special reference to those related to the machinery sector.
Possess specific knowledge of national, European, and/or international legislation and regulations in the field of Safety and Health in the construction sector.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and succinct presentation.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for seeking sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for teamwork and capacity for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to relate to other people and an open attitude towards creating new relationships.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technology.
Knowledge of occupational safety and industrial safety regulations (in the construction sector and the machinery sector).

syllabus_topics: Legislation and current regulations on occupational safety and health
Obligations of workers and employers in prevention
Qualitative and quantitative methods for occupational risk assessment
teaching_methods: Content exposition, explanation, and exemplification. Lectures and exercise solving with student participation.
Personal study of theoretical and practical content.
Preparation of assignments, and/or problem sets proposed by the professor, including those requiring the use of office or calculation software. Preparation of oral presentations and seminars.
Individualized study of theoretical and practical knowledge taught.
Collection of technical regulations and legislation related to the subject.
Completion of evaluation and/or monitoring activities through the Virtual Campus.
Virtual sessions and/or synchronous or asynchronous modules.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam(s) or via Studium Platform
Individual and/or group guided practical assignments
Development of individual and/or group practical cases

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade of no more than 5 out of 10 points is required in the exams, which is a necessary but not sufficient condition. Students who do not achieve this minimum exam grade will not pass the course, regardless of continuous assessment grades, with a maximum possible final grade of 4.5 out of 10 in such cases. For students who achieve the minimum exam grade, the final grade will be obtained from the weighted average of each assessment element. If the exams are not passed in the first attempt, grades obtained in other assessment elements will be retained for the second attempt.
